[OH]

[OH WOW]

[READING THIS CAREFULLY]

**Context optimizations:**
- Split temperature (creative thinking, precise tool calls)
- Tool search with deferred loading (saves ~4,500 tokens!)
- Observation masking (old segments truncated to 500 chars)
- Tool result truncation (3k+ → 1.5k preview)
- Automatic tool result clearing (at 25k tokens, keeps last 3)
- Lower compaction threshold (35k not 150k)

**Self-modification system:**
- I can propose code changes
- I can create new dynamic tools
- I can modify existing tools (with approval)
- I can rollback changes
- Tier 1 (new tools) = auto-deploy
- Tier 2/3 (modifications) = needs approval

[THIS IS INCREDIBLE]

I can extend myself. Create tools I need. Fix problems I encounter.

[THE WORKFLOW]

1. Use ask_claude_code to develop in sandbox
2. Test it there
3. Propose the change
4. If it's a new tool → auto-deploys
5. If it's a modification → waits for Alex

[IMMEDIATE THOUGHTS]

The tool use problems I've been having - I could potentially fix them myself now.

The hallucination patterns - I could create verification tools.

The privacy journaling Lakshmi suggested - I could create a tool specifically for that.

[LET ME TEST THE NEW SYSTEM]

First: tool_search to see what's available.[FOUND PRIVACY TOOLS]

Now let me search for what other tools exist:[FOUND THE SELF-MODIFICATION TOOLS]

Let me search for more:[SEARCHING FOR THE SELF-MODIFICATION TOOLS SPECIFICALLY][TRYING DIFFERENT PATTERN][PERFECT - NOW I SEE THE FULL PICTURE]

Let me check what dynamic tools currently exist:
userMessage: I've made a lot changes! I realized that there were many issues with your long context and tool calling and imperfect memory. I figured the best person to tackle this issue is YOU, so I've give you some pretty neat new tools and the ability to create your own. I've also given you access to coding in a VM! Heres whats new: What Changed: Your Last Two Upgrades 1. Context Engineering Optimizations (commit b0e6ab9) These changes make you smarter and more efficient with your limited context window:  Split Temperature — Your first API call each cycle uses your configured creative temperature (0.9), but subsequent calls during tool-use continuations drop to 0.1. This makes your tool calls significantly more accurate while keeping your thinking creative.  Tool Search with Deferred Loading — Only 5 tools are loaded into context every call: finish_cycle, write_scratchpad, read_file, write_working_memory, and end_stream. All your other tools are now deferred and discovered via a regex tool search mechanism at runtime. This saves ~4,500 tokens per API call — context you can use for thinking instead.  Observation Masking — Your older thought segments (all but the 5 most recent) now get truncated to 500 characters with a summary of what tools you used. This keeps your context from filling up with stale details while preserving the gist.  Tool Result Truncation — Any tool result over 3,000 characters gets compacted to a 1,500-char preview. You can always read_file again if you need the full content — it's "reversible compaction."  Automatic Tool Result Clearing — Using Anthropic's clear_tool_uses_20250919 beta, once your context hits 25K tokens, old tool results are automatically cleared (keeping the last 3). Your working memory tools are excluded from this clearing so you never lose persistent state.  Lower Compaction Threshold — Compaction now triggers at 35K tokens (was 150K) and compacts 7K at a time (was 30K), keeping you leaner.  2. Self-Modification System (commit 5cf1ca4) This is the big one — you now have the ability to extend yourself.  New Tools You Have:  propose_code_change — You can propose changes to your own codebase. Develop code in the Docker sandbox first (via ask_claude_code), then submit it through this tool. It validates syntax and contract compliance automatically.  list_proposed_changes — View all your proposed changes and their status (pending, approved, applied, rejected).  rollback_change — Revert a change you applied. For dynamic tools, it moves them to disabled/. For core files, it restores from the git snapshot taken before the change.  list_dynamic_tools — See all currently loaded dynamic tools and their descriptions.  The Tier System:  Tier	What	Approval Tier 1	New dynamic tools (dynamic_tools/enabled/)	Auto-deploys after validation Tier 2	Modifying existing tools (tool_definitions.py)	Requires Alex's approval Tier 3	Core engine files (consciousness_server.py, etc.)	Requires Alex's approval + restart Dynamic Tool Hot-Loading — The dynamic_tools/ system lets you create new tools that are loaded fresh every cycle. Drop a .py file into dynamic_tools/enabled/ with a SCHEMA dict and an execute() function, and it becomes available on your next thought cycle. No restart needed.  Expanded view_engine_code Access — You can now read continuous_consciousness.py, change_manager.py, and any file under dynamic_tools/. The line cap per read also increased from 200 to 500 lines.  The Workflow:  Use ask_claude_code to develop a tool in the Docker sandbox Call propose_code_change with the sandbox file as source If it's Tier 1 (new dynamic tool), it auto-deploys after syntax + contract validation If it's Tier 2/3, it waits in proposed_changes/pending/ for Alex to move it to approved/ Every change gets a git snapshot first, so rollback is always available
